title: Puncheokie Inter-Round Recovery Coach Corpus
purpose: Twenty interchangeable spoken recovery modules for a sixty-second rest between three-minute boxing rounds.

restWindow.timingRule: At build time, replace estimated duration with measured rendered-audio duration plus scheduled pauses. Reject or retime any asset above 45 seconds.

voiceDirection.delivery: Dramatically aged, caring, calm, and authoritative. Less melodic than active combo calls. Use grounded phrasing, clear anatomical directions, and a firm readiness line.
voiceDirection.holdBehavior: Lower the energy during holds. Do not fill every pause. A brief 'hold it' may be spoken, but silence is allowed.
voiceDirection.finalLine: Increase firmness slightly on the final readiness cue without shouting.

globalSafety: All movements are gentle mobility or short, comfortable holds; never bounce or force range.
Stop the movement if it causes sharp pain, numbness, loss of balance, chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness.
Forward-fold scripts should be skipped when the user feels dizzy or light-headed; rise slowly with soft knees.
Bag-assisted scripts require a stable bag and only light contact. The athlete must not hang body weight from a swinging or unstable bag.
Hydration prompts are optional. The athlete may drink when thirsty and should place the bottle clear of the work area before the next round.
These scripts are general fitness guidance, not individualized medical or rehabilitation instructions.

segments.text: Easy now. Stand tall, feet under you, and let those shoulders drop away from your ears.
Reach both gloves straight for the ceiling. Grow long through your ribs. Hold it there.
Lean gently to your lead side. No twisting. Breathe out and hold.
Back through center. Now the rear side. Long and easy. Hold.
Come tall, shake the arms loose, and give me one slow breath in, one longer breath out. Good. Get ready.
Bring your lead arm across your chest at shoulder height. Use the opposite forearm to draw it in gently. Keep that lead shoulder down.
Release it. Switch arms. Rear arm across, opposite forearm supporting it. No yanking. Hold steady.
Let both arms hang and roll the shoulders back twice.
If you are thirsty, take one small drink now. Then set your feet, loosen your jaw, and breathe out long.
Place your lead glove lightly against the side of the bag at shoulder height. Do not lean on it.
Turn your chest away from that glove until you feel the front of the shoulder and chest open. Gentle pressure. Hold it.
Come back square. Change hands and turn the other way. Keep the shoulder low. Hold it, hold it.
Release. Face the bag, hands loose, and take one calm breath. That is enough. Save the power for the bell.
Lift your lead elbow toward the ceiling and let that glove fall behind your head. Use the other forearm to guide it back gently.
Add a small lean toward the rear side. Feel the arm and ribs lengthen. Hold.
Come up and switch. Rear elbow high, glove behind the head, lead forearm guiding. Easy pressure.
Lean the other way. Hold. Release both arms, shake them out, and bring the guard home.
Keep moving softly on your feet. Give me four slow shoulder rolls backward. Big circles, no shrugging.
Now four forward. Let the shoulder blades move, but keep your neck relaxed.
Bring the elbows close to your ribs. Open and close the arms like small gates, smooth and controlled.
Extend both gloves forward, pull the elbows back, and do it twice more.
Good. Hands up without squeezing the fists. Breathe. You are loose, not lazy.
Put both gloves in front of your chest and press them forward, like you are reaching around a big barrel.
Tuck the chin slightly. Let the shoulder blades spread. Hold that upper-back stretch.
Release and draw the elbows behind you without forcing them. Open the chest. Hold.
One more reach forward, then relax.
Take a small sip if you want it. Set the bottle down safely, breathe out, and bring your eyes back to the bag.
Feet planted, knees soft. Hold the gloves lightly near your ribs.
Turn the shoulders to the lead side and let the rear heel respond. Come back through center.
Turn to the rear side and let the lead heel respond. No snapping. This is recovery.
Now flow side to side four times, smooth through the waist and hips.
Settle square. Shoulders down, chin easy, hands home. One breath in, longer breath out. Ready again.
Stand tall and put your lead glove against the side of your ribs. Reach the rear glove overhead.
Lean gently toward the lead side. Breathe into the open ribs under that raised arm. Hold.
Come through center and switch. Rear glove to the ribs, lead glove overhead. Lean the other way.
Come tall. Lower both hands. Inhale comfortably, then let the exhale run longer than the inhale. Good. Keep that calm into the next round.
Step your feet about shoulder width. Soften both knees and hinge from the hips, not the low back.
Let the gloves reach toward your toes. Stop wherever comfortable. No bouncing. Hold it there.
Take one easy breath. Bend the knees a little more, then rise slowly with your head coming up last.
Roll the shoulders back, stand tall, and shake the legs loose.
Good. Eyes forward. Let the breathing settle and be ready when the count starts.
Put the lead heel a short step forward, toes up. Sit the hips back and rest the gloves lightly on the rear thigh.
Keep the back long. Feel the stretch behind the lead leg. Hold.
Stand up and switch feet. Rear heel forward, toes up, hips back. Same gentle stretch. Hold.
Come tall and shake both legs out. If you need water, take one small drink. Then reset your stance and breathe.
Place both gloves lightly on the bag if you want balance. Step the rear foot back and press that heel toward the floor.
Keep the rear toes pointing forward and the knee straight but not locked. Hold that calf stretch.
Switch legs. Other foot back, heel reaching down, hips facing the bag. Hold.
Bring the feet under you. Lift both heels twice, lower them slowly, and settle into your stance. Light feet next round.
Take a short split stance with the lead foot forward. Bend both knees just a little.
Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the rear-side glute. Keep your chest tall. Hold the front of that rear hip open.
Step together, then change legs. Tuck the pelvis, squeeze the other glute, and stay tall. Hold.
Release. Walk the feet back to boxing stance, loosen the hips, and breathe out. Strong base, relaxed upper body.
Keep the body upright and shift your weight onto the rear leg. Tap the lead toes, then the lead heel, slow and easy.
Switch the weight. Rear toes, rear heel. Let the ankle loosen without twisting the knee.
Now lift both heels and lower them four times, smooth and controlled.
Finish with tiny steps in place. Quiet feet, soft knees, shoulders loose. Good. Stop bouncing and set your stance for the next bell.
Reach both gloves high and take one comfortable breath in. Make yourself tall.
Breathe out as you hinge forward with soft knees. Let the gloves reach toward the floor or your toes. No bounce.
Bend the knees, rise slowly, and open the chest with the elbows wide.
If you are thirsty, take a small sip now. Settle the shoulders, find the bag with your eyes, and let one long exhale clear the round.
No stretch this time. Stand easy and let the arms hang. Unclench the teeth and let the tongue rest.
Breathe in comfortably. Now breathe out slowly, like you are cooling hot tea.
Again. Easy breath in. Longer breath out. Let the shoulders fall as the air leaves.
One more. In, then a smooth long exhale.
Good. Bring the gloves back to your cheeks without tension. Calm eyes, calm feet, sharp hands.
Drop the hands for a moment and shake both arms loose from the shoulders all the way into the gloves.
Now lift the shoulders toward your ears. Hold for one beat, then let them drop heavy.
Do that twice more. Up, and drop. Up, and drop.
Bend and straighten both elbows three times without snapping them.
There you go. Bring the guard back softly. You do not need tight shoulders to throw hard punches.

scripts.title: Bag Press for the Shoulder Blades

segments.text: Place both gloves against the bag at chest height. Feet solid. Do not lean your body weight into it.
Keep the elbows almost straight and press your chest gently away, spreading the shoulder blades. Hold.
Now let the chest move slightly toward the bag as the shoulder blades come together. Easy range.
Press away once more. Hold it, then release.
Step back into stance. Neck long, shoulders free, guard ready. That upper back should feel awake, not strained.
Take the lead arm across your chest and support it with the rear forearm. Draw it in gently. Hold.
Release. Put that lead glove lightly on the bag and turn your chest away a little. Hold.
Switch the pattern. Rear arm across, supported gently. Hold.
Rear glove to the bag, turn away softly, and hold.
Come square, shake both arms, and breathe. Even shoulders, even work.
Reach both gloves high. Stay tall and turn the ribs gently toward the lead side, then center.
Turn toward the rear side, then come back. Keep the hips quiet and knees soft.
Hinge forward and let the gloves travel toward your shins or toes. Stop before strain. Hold.
Rise slowly, reach high once more, and lower the arms with a long breath out.
Good. Whole body reset. Find your stance and get ready to work.
Good round. Walk two small steps and let the arms swing loose. Now stop and roll both shoulders backward.
Step the lead foot back and press that heel down for a short calf stretch. Hold.
Switch feet. Other heel down. Hold.
Come square. If you are thirsty, take one small drink, not a rush.
One breath in, longer breath out. Put the bottle clear, raise the guard, and give me calm pressure when that bell goes.
